svg.title: Source exchange: exact accumulation removes order dependence
svg.desc: A binary categorical system whose synergy differed in the final bit when two sources were exchanged under compensated summation. Exact accumulation of the represented terms makes both orders agree; the shared value lies three units in the last place below the exact functional value.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: SOURCE EXCHANGE: EXACT ACCUMULATION REMOVES ORDER DEPENDENCE
Binary categorical MGW, (S1, S2) about T: counts (c000, …, c111) = (0,1,1,1,2,1,5,1); n = 12.
Swapping two tiny terms rounded the correction to exactly half a unit. The
tie lowered the misinformative sum by one unit and raised the synergy by
Each finite operand is an integer multiple of 2−1074.
Storage includes the bounded term-count carry.
2 × 34 = 68 limbs in total; no intermediate rounding.
Subtract the exact signed magnitudes, then
round to nearest binary64, ties to even.
Both source orders: same synergy payload
Source: the recorded pid-rs source-exchange witness. Exact reduction concerns represented operands; values are in nats.
